newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals end dull day mostly firmer.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals end dull day mostly firmer.

text.p: Yen-based precious metals futures settled mostly firmer in dull trade on Friday, aligning themselves with overnight levels in otherwise featureless trade, dealers said.
The market also received no direction from the yen/dollar rate, which held mostly steady after the yen's recent weakening toward the 110 per dollar level.
Most-active August 1997 gold settled three yen firmer at 1,343 yen per gram after trading narrowly from 1,344 to 1,341, while the other contracts were flat to five yen higher.

December gold maintained its premium to the other months, ending four up at 1,356, lifted by trade house short-covering as many individual investors on the long side of the market held on to their positions rather than rolling them forward.
"Every year there's always something strange in the December contract," one trade house source said.
Gold bullion settled at $385.50/80 an ounce, largely unchanged from New York's closing quote of $385.50/$386.00 and off slightly from Tokyo's Thursday close at $385.90/$386.40.
Traders said the loco Tokyo premium had mostly recovered to normal levels after slipping into a discount early in the week.

One trader blamed the slump on bar sales from South Korea, after a recent change in gold dealing regulations there, and selling by a trade house that took delivery of a large volume of bullion at last week's expiry of the August contract.
He quoted the premium at 1.5 yen per gram (about 43 cents an ounce) over loco London, near levels seen early last week.

In the other precious metals, August 1997 platinum ended one yen better at 1,368 yen per gram, August 1997 silver rose 0.3 yen to 183.2 yen per 10 grams and August 1997 palladium was up one yen at 440 yen per gram.
